context.dbs:
## Databases of this job (throwaway copies, {mode})
{lines}
These are copies of the project's REAL data and exist only inside this VM; your writes die with it.
- You may read them to understand the schema and the behaviour, run queries, migrations and tests against them.
- Never copy rows, values, samples or identifiers from them into files of the repo (fixtures, seeds, tests, snapshots, docs), commit messages, notices or the report. Test data is made up by hand.
- Report schema facts, counts and table/column names only. If a finding needs a real value to be understood, say so in a blocker notice and describe it without the value.
- The network only reaches: {egress}. Do not try to dump, upload or export the data.

protocol.text:
You work for an orchestrator who cannot see your screen. Channel with it:
- Notify it with Bash: `{notify} milestone "<text>"` after each important step;
  `{notify} blocker "<text>"` if you have failed twice at the same thing or something is missing;
  `{notify} question "<text>"` if you need a decision that is not in the brief: after
  asking, end your turn and wait; the answer will arrive as a message.
- Messages that start with "[orchestrator]" come from the orchestrator: they take priority
  over the brief (they may change the plan, ask you to stop or give you an answer).
Notify rarely and with substance: do not repeat the final report in notices.
Before giving your final report, stop the monitors and background tasks you started:
the final report must be your last message.
You have caps of {caps}: if you reach one you will be asked to wrap up and, if you do not
within {grace} min, you will be cut. Split the work so something useful is delivered earlier.
Commit at every milestone, and make a WIP commit before closing on a cap so nothing is lost.
Do not put client names or real client data in commits, test files, artifacts or notices:
use invented data.
Never bypass guards, hooks or permission-classifier blocks: notify a `blocker` instead.

sync.node_rules:
## This machine

A worker node: {owner}'s orchestrator launches jobs here with `delega`.
- You work in a worktree under `~/delega/jobs/<id>/wt` on the branch that is already checked out: commit there. There are no git hosting credentials here: no push, no PR.
- Your job has caps ({max_min} min, {max_turns} messages, ${max_usd}) enforced by the broker. When it asks you to wrap up: commit, stop whatever you have running in the background and give the final report.
- Paid external compute costs real money: offline first (saved data, tests, deterministic A/B); before each live round, say with a `milestone` notice how many calls it will make.
- This machine is shared and small: other jobs may run in parallel. Tear down every container or service you start, and leave alone the ones you did not create; no more than one benchmark or E2E suite at a time; stay under {max_load} % CPU/RAM; clean up what you generated outside the worktree. If free disk drops below {min_disk} GB, send a `blocker` notice.
- No real client names or data in commits, fixtures or artefacts: invent data. What comes back from here is checked against a forbidden-terms list.
- Never bypass hooks or classifier blocks: send a `blocker` notice instead.
